keyVerseText: And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age , and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity;
rootMeaning: The name Ἄννα (Ánna) is of Hebrew origin, derived from חַנָּה (Channâh), which means "grace." This root conveys a sense of favor and kindness, suggesting that the bearer of the name is associated with divine grace or a gracious character. Understanding this root enriches the common English use of the name Anna by highlighting its deep connection to the concept of God’s unmerited favor and blessing.
usageInScripture: The word Ἄννα appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Luke 2:36, where it refers to a prophetess named Anna. The singular occurrence and translation as "one Anna" indicate that it is a proper name rather than a common noun. This consistent use as a personal name reflects the historical and cultural significance of Anna as an individual known for her prophetic role and devotion.
theologicalSignificance: The original meaning of Anna as "grace" is theologically significant because it points to the embodiment of God’s favor in a faithful servant. Anna’s role as a prophetess in Scripture underscores how grace is not only a divine attribute but also something manifested in the lives of those who faithfully serve God. Her presence in Luke’s gospel highlights the continuity of God’s gracious work from the Old Testament into the New Testament era, ultimately fulfilled in Christ. Recognizing Anna’s name as rooted in grace encourages believers to see their own lives as recipients and reflectors of God’s unmerited favor.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 2:36 introduces Anna as a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel from the tribe of Asher, emphasizing her advanced age and lifelong dedication to God. The use of the name Ἄννα here connects her identity directly to the concept of grace, inviting readers to see her prophetic ministry as an expression of God’s gracious revelation. This verse portrays Anna not just as a historical figure but as a living testament to God’s enduring grace and faithfulness throughout her life.
